title: Posterior concentration and adaptation of the mixing measure in Dirichlet process mixtures
summary: We study the asymptotic properties of the posterior on the latent space for infinite mixtures driven by a Dirichlet process, both in terms of mixing measure and clustering behaviour. In the well-specified regime, where the data are generated by a finite mixture of location densities, we show that the posterior is adaptive to the true number of components $K$: indeed the cumulative mass assigned to weights of the stick-breaking representation beyond the $K$-th one vanishes as $n^{-1/2}$, up to terms growing slower than any polynomial.
